title.raw: 卷七十九 列傳第六十九 夷貊下 Volume 79 Biographies 69: Non-Han Peoples 2

sentences.zh: 東夷 西戎 蠻 西域諸國 蠕蠕

translations.literal: Eastern Yi, Western Rong, Man, states of the Western Regions, Rouran
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yi, Western Rong, Man, Western Regions, and Rouran

translations.literal: 1.1.1 Koguryo
translations.idiomatic: 1.1.1 Koguryo

translations.literal: 1.1.2 Baekje
translations.idiomatic: 1.1.2 Baekje

translations.literal: 1.1.3 Silla
translations.idiomatic: 1.1.3 Silla

sentences.zh: 東夷之國，朝鮮為大，得箕子之化，其器物猶有禮樂云。

translations.literal: Among the states of the Eastern Yi, Korea is greatest; it received Gija's transformation, and its vessels still preserve ritual and music, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Eastern Yi, Korea is greatest; civilized by Gija, its vessels still keep ritual and music, they say.

sentences.zh: 魏時，朝鮮以東馬韓、辰韓之屬，世通中國。

translations.literal: In Wei times, east of Korea the Ma Han, Jin Han, and the like communicated with China generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, Ma Han, Jin Han, and others east of Korea traded with China generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 自晉過江，泛海來使，有高句麗、百濟，而宋、齊間常通職貢，梁興又有加焉。

translations.literal: After Jin crossed the Yangzi, sea envoys came—among them Koguryo and Baekje; under Song and Qi they often sent tribute and office; when Liang rose, there was increase still.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin crossed the river, Koguryo and Baekje sent sea envoys; under Song and Qi they often paid tribute, and when Liang arose contact increased further.

sentences.zh: 扶桑國，在昔未聞也，梁普通中有道人稱自彼而至，其言元本尤悉，故並錄焉。

translations.literal: Fusang—in former times it was unheard of; in the Putong era of Liang a monk claimed to have come from there; his original account was especially thorough, and so it is recorded together here.
translations.idiomatic: Fusang was unknown in former times; in Liang's Putong era a monk claimed to come from there, and his account was unusually full, so it is recorded here as well.

sentences.zh: 高句麗

translations.literal: Koguryo
translations.idiomatic: Koguryo

sentences.zh: 高句麗，在遼東之東千里，其先所出，事詳北史。

translations.literal: Koguryo lies a thousand li east of Liaodong; the origin of its ruling house is given in detail in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryo stands a thousand li east of Liaodong; its royal origins are treated fully in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 地方可二千里，中有遼山，遼水所出。

translations.literal: Its territory was about two thousand li; within it is Liaoshan, whence the Liaoshui flows.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm covered some two thousand li; Liaoshan rises there, source of the Liaoshui.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏世，南與朝鮮獩貊、東與沃沮、北與夫餘接。

translations.literal: In Han and Wei times it bordered Korea, the Hui tribes, and the Mo to the south, Wolu to the east, and Buyeo to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Wei it touched Korea, Hui, and Mo in the south, Wolu in the east, and Buyeo in the north.

sentences.zh: 其王都於丸都山下，地多大山深谷，無原澤，百姓依之以居，食澗水。

translations.literal: The king's capital was below Wandu Mountain; there were many great mountains and deep valleys, no plains or marshes; the people lived along the slopes and drank stream water.
translations.idiomatic: The king's seat lay below Wandu Mountain amid great mountains and deep valleys without plains; people clung to the slopes and drank from streams.

sentences.zh: 雖土著，無良田，故其俗節食，好修宮室。

translations.literal: Though settled, they had no good farmland; therefore their custom was to eat sparingly, and they liked to build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Though settled, they lacked good fields; so they ate frugally and loved grand buildings.

sentences.zh: 于所居之左立大屋，祭鬼神，又祠零星、社稷。

translations.literal: To the left of where they dwelt they raised a great hall to sacrifice to ghosts and spirits, and also worshipped the scattered stars and the soil-altar.
translations.idiomatic: Left of each dwelling stood a hall for ghost and spirit sacrifice, and for worship of scattered stars and the soil-altar.

sentences.zh: 人性凶急，喜寇鈔。

translations.literal: By nature they were fierce and hasty, fond of raiding and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and hasty by nature, they loved raiding and plunder.

sentences.zh: 其官有相加、對盧、沛者、古鄒加、主簿、優台、使者、皁衣、先人，尊卑各有等級。

translations.literal: Their offices included xiangjia, duilu, peizhe, guzoujia, chief clerk, youtai, envoy, zaoyi, and xianren—high and low each had rank.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included xiangjia, duilu, peizhe, guzoujia, chief clerk, youtai, envoy, zaoyi, and xianren—each rank had its place.

sentences.zh: 言語諸事，多與夫餘同，其性氣衣服有異。

translations.literal: In speech and affairs they mostly resembled Buyeo; in temperament and dress they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Speech and custom mostly matched Buyeo; temperament and dress differed.

sentences.zh: 本有五族，有消奴部、絕奴部、慎奴部、灌奴部、桂婁部。

translations.literal: Originally there were five clans: the Xiaonu, Juenu, Shennu, Guannu, and Guilou.
translations.idiomatic: Five clans originally ruled: Xiaonu, Juenu, Shennu, Guannu, and Guilou.

sentences.zh: 本消奴部為王，微弱，桂婁部代之。

translations.literal: Originally the Xiaonu clan held kingship; weakened, the Guilou clan replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Xiaonu clan held the throne; when they weakened, the Guilou clan replaced them.

sentences.zh: 其置官，有對盧則不置沛者，有沛者則不置對盧。

translations.literal: In appointing offices, if there is a duilu there is no peizhe; if there is a peizhe there is no duilu.
translations.idiomatic: In office, duilu and peizhe are not appointed together—where one stands, the other is omitted.

sentences.zh: 俗喜歌舞，國中邑落，男女每夜群聚歌戲。

translations.literal: Their custom loves song and dance; in settlements throughout the state, men and women each night gather in groups to sing and play.
translations.idiomatic: They love song and dance; in every settlement men and women gather nightly to sing and play.

sentences.zh: 其人潔淨自喜，善藏釀，跪拜申一腳，行步皆走。

translations.literal: The people are clean and self-pleasing, skilled at brewing liquor; in bowing they extend one foot; in walking and in steps they always run.
translations.idiomatic: They are fastidious and proud of cleanliness, skilled at brewing; they kowtow on one foot and walk and run at a trot.

sentences.zh: 以十月祭天大會。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they hold a great assembly to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they hold a great heaven-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其公會衣服皆錦繡金銀以自飾，大加、主簿頭所著似幘而無後，其小加著折風，形如弁。

translations.literal: At public assemblies their clothes are all brocade and gold and silver for self-adornment; the great xiang and the chief clerk wear on the head something like a cap but without a back; lesser xiang wear zhefeng, shaped like a bian cap.
translations.idiomatic: At public assemblies all dress in brocade and gold and silver; great xiang and chief clerks wear headgear like a cap but without a back, while lesser xiang wear zhefeng caps shaped like court bian.

sentences.zh: 其國無牢獄，有罪者則會諸加評議，重者便殺之，沒入其妻子。

translations.literal: The state has no prisons; when someone is guilty, the various xiang assemble to discuss; the serious cases are put to death at once, and wife and children are confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: There are no prisons; the guilty are judged in council by the xiang; serious offenders are killed at once and their wives and children seized.

sentences.zh: 其俗好淫，男女多相奔誘。

translations.literal: Their custom favors licentiousness; men and women often elope and seduce one another.
translations.idiomatic: They are licentious by custom; men and women often run off together in mutual seduction.

sentences.zh: 已嫁娶便稍作送終之衣。

translations.literal: Once married, they soon make slight preparations for burial garments.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage they quickly begin preparing modest burial clothes.

sentences.zh: 其死葬，有槨無棺。

translations.literal: In death and burial, they have outer coffins but no inner coffins.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are buried in outer coffins without inner coffins.

sentences.zh: 好厚葬，金銀財幣盡於送死。

translations.literal: They favor lavish burial; gold, silver, and currency are all spent on the dead.
translations.idiomatic: They love lavish funerals and pour gold, silver, and coin into the dead.

sentences.zh: 積石為封，列植松柏。

translations.literal: They pile stones for the tomb mound and plant pine and cypress in rows.
translations.idiomatic: Stone mounds mark the graves, with pine and cypress planted in rows.

sentences.zh: 兄死妻嫂。

translations.literal: When an elder brother dies, the younger brother takes the widow as wife.
translations.idiomatic: A younger brother takes his dead elder brother's widow as wife.

sentences.zh: 其馬皆小，便登山。

translations.literal: Their horses are all small, suited for climbing mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses are small and nimble on mountain paths.

sentences.zh: 國人尚氣力，便弓矢刀矛，有鎧甲，習戰鬥，沃沮、東濊皆屬焉。

translations.literal: The people value physical strength and are skilled with bow, arrow, blade, and spear; they have armor and practice warfare; Wolu and Eastern Hui all belong to them.
translations.idiomatic: The people honor strength and excel with bow, arrow, blade, and spear; they wear armor and train for battle; Wolu and Eastern Hui are subject to them.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙九年，高麗王高璉遣長史高翼奉表，獻赭白馬，晉以璉為使持節、都督營州諸軍事、征東將軍、高麗王、樂浪公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi under Jin Emperor An, King Gao Lian of Goguryo sent Chief Clerk Gao Yi with a memorial, presenting chestnut and white horses; Jin made Lian Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Ying Province, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryo, and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin An's ninth Yixi year, Goguryo King Gao Lian sent Chief Clerk Gao Yi with a memorial and chestnut-and-white horses; Jin made him Bearer of the Staff, commander of Ying Province military affairs, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryo, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝踐阼，加璉征東大將軍，余官並如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song took the throne, Lian was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the East; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Song's Emperor Wu ascended, Lian was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the East; his other offices stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 三年，加璉散騎常侍，增督平州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year, Lian was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, with added supervision of military affairs in Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Lian became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and gained supervision of Ping Province military affairs.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，璉遣長史馬婁等來獻方物，遣謁者朱邵伯、王邵子等慰勞之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under Emperor Shao, Lian sent Chief Clerk Ma Lou and others to present local products; the court dispatched Attendants Zhu Shaobo and Wang Shaozi and others to console and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: In Shao's second Jingping year Lian sent Chief Clerk Ma Lou with local goods; Attendants Zhu Shaobo and Wang Shaozi and others were sent to console them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十五年，馮弘為魏所攻，敗奔高麗北豐城，表求迎接。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, Feng Hong was attacked by Wei, defeated, and fled to Beifeng city in Goguryo, submitting a memorial requesting reception.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia fifteen Feng Hong, attacked by Wei, fled defeated to Beifeng in Goguryo and asked to be received.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣使王白駒、趙次興迎之，並令高麗資遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen dispatched envoys Wang Baiju and Zhao Cixing to welcome him, and also ordered Goguryo to supply provisions for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Wang Baiju and Zhao Cixing to welcome him and ordered Goguryo to provide travel supplies.

sentences.zh: 璉不欲弘南，乃遣將孫漱、高仇等襲殺之。

translations.literal: Lian did not wish Feng Hong to go south, and so sent generals Sun Shu and Gao Chou and others to attack and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lian did not want Hong to go south and sent generals Sun Shu and Gao Chou and others to kill him.

sentences.zh: 白駒等率所領七千餘人生禽漱，殺仇等二人。

translations.literal: Baiju and others at the head of more than seven thousand men living-captured Shu and killed Chou and two others.
translations.idiomatic: Baiju and his more than seven thousand men captured Shu alive and killed Chou and two others.

sentences.zh: 璉以白駒等專殺，遣使執送之。

translations.literal: Lian, because Baiju and others had killed on their own authority, sent envoys to seize and deliver them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, holding that Baiju and others had killed without authorization, sent envoys to seize and deliver them.

sentences.zh: 上以遠國不欲違其意，白駒等下獄見原。

translations.literal: The Emperor, not wishing to go against the wishes of a distant state, had Baiju and others imprisoned but then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, unwilling to offend a distant realm, imprisoned Baiju and the others but then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 璉每歲遣使。

translations.literal: Lian sent envoys every year.
translations.idiomatic: Lian sent envoys every year.

sentences.zh: 十六年，文帝欲侵魏，詔璉送馬，獻八百匹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Emperor Wen wished to attack Wei and ordered Lian to send horses; eight hundred were presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Emperor Wen planned to attack Wei and ordered horses from Lian; eight hundred were sent.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建二年，璉遣長史董騰奉表，慰國哀再周，並獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Lian sent Chief Clerk Dong Teng with a memorial comforting the court on the completion of the second mourning cycle, and also presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowu's second Xiaojian year Lian sent Chief Clerk Dong Teng with a memorial of condolence for the second mourning cycle and local goods.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，又獻肅慎氏楛矢石砮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he again presented Sushen clan hardwood arrows and stone arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming two he again sent Sushen hardwood arrows and stone arrowheads.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔進璉為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，餘官並如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict advanced Lian to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict made Lian General of Chariots and Cavalry with Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies and an opening office; other offices stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始、後廢帝元徽中，貢獻不絕，曆齊並授爵位，百餘歲死。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming's Taishi and Emperor Houfei's Yuanhui eras, tribute never ceased; through Qi he received ranks and titles; he died aged over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming's Taishi and Houfei's Yuanhui tribute never ceased; Qi too granted him rank; he died past a hundred.

sentences.zh: 子雲立，齊隆昌中，以為使持節、散騎常侍、都督營平二州、征東大將軍、高麗王、樂浪公。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded; in Longchang of Qi he was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of Ying and Ping two provinces, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, in Qi Longchang, became Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of Ying and Ping, General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝即位，進雲車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, Yun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu ascended, Yun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天監七年，詔為撫東大將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、常侍、都督、王並如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian, an edict made him General Who Pacifies the East, Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander, and kingship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian seven an edict made him General Who Pacifies the East with Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies and an opening office; staff, attendant, command, and kingship were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十一年、十五年，累遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and fifteenth years, envoys were repeatedly sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh and fifteenth years they sent tribute envoys again and again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，雲死，子安立。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yun died; his son An succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yun died and his son An succeeded.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，詔安纂襲封爵，持節、督營平二州諸軍事、甯東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong, an edict had An inherit the enfeoffment and rank: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Ying and Ping two provinces, General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong one an edict had An inherit the title: Bearer of the Staff, commander of Ying and Ping military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 七年，安卒，子延立，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, An died; his son Yan succeeded; envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year An died; his son Yan succeeded and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 詔以延襲爵。

translations.literal: An edict had Yan inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Yan inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年、六年，大同元年、七年，累奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth and sixth years of Zhongdatong, and the first and seventh years of Datong, memorials and local products were repeatedly offered.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong four and six and Datong one and seven they repeatedly sent memorials and local goods.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，延卒，詔其子成襲延爵位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Yan died; an edict had his son Cheng inherit Yan's title and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing two Yan died; an edict had his son Cheng inherit Yan's title.

sentences.zh: 百濟者，其先東夷有三韓國：一曰馬韓，二曰辰韓，三曰弁韓。

translations.literal: Baekje—in antiquity among the Eastern Yi there were three Han states: the first called Ma Han, the second Jin Han, the third Byeon Han.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje arose among the Eastern Yi's three Han realms—Ma Han, Jin Han, and Byeon Han.

sentences.zh: 弁韓、辰韓各十二國，馬韓有五十四國。

translations.literal: Byeon Han and Jin Han each had twelve states; Ma Han had fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Byeon Han and Jin Han held twelve states each; Ma Han held fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 大國萬餘家，小國數千家，總十餘萬戶，百濟即其一也。

translations.literal: Large states had over ten thousand households, small ones several thousand; altogether over a hundred thousand households—Baekje was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Great states held ten thousand households or more, small ones a few thousand—over a hundred thousand households in all; Baekje was one.

sentences.zh: 後漸強大，兼諸小國。

translations.literal: Later it gradually grew powerful and absorbed the smaller states.
translations.idiomatic: Later it grew strong and swallowed the lesser states.

sentences.zh: 其國本與句麗俱在遼東之東千餘里，晉世句麗既略有遼東，百濟亦據有遼西、晉平二郡地矣，自置百濟郡。

translations.literal: Its state originally lay a thousand-odd li east of Liaodong with Koguryo; in Jin times, once Koguryo had occupied Liaodong, Baekje also held the territory of Liaoxi and Jinping two commanderies and established its own Baekje commandery.
translations.idiomatic: It once lay a thousand-odd li east of Liaodong with Koguryo; when Koguryo seized Liaodong in Jin, Baekje took Liaoxi and Jinping and set up its own Baekje commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉義熙十二年，以百濟王餘映為使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi under Jin, King Yu Ying of Baekje was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's twelfth Yixi year Baekje King Yu Ying became Bearer of the Staff, commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝踐阼，進號鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song took the throne, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Song's Emperor Wu ascended, his title rose to Grand General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，映遣長史張威詣闕貢獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under Emperor Shao, Ying sent Chief Clerk Zhang Wei to the court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Shao's second Jingping year Ying sent Chief Clerk Zhang Wei to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，文帝詔兼謁者閭丘恩子、兼副謁者丁敬子等往宣旨慰勞，其後每歲遣使奉獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Emperor Wen ordered Acting Attendant Qiu Enzi and Acting Deputy Attendant Ding Jingzi and others to proclaim the imperial will and console them; afterward envoys were sent every year with local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia two Emperor Wen sent Acting Attendant Qiu Enzi and Acting Deputy Attendant Ding Jingzi and others to proclaim the imperial will and console them; thereafter envoys came yearly with local goods.

sentences.zh: 七年，百濟王余毗復修貢職，以映爵號授之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, King Yu Bi of Baekje again restored tribute duties; Ying's enfeoffment and title were conferred on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Baekje King Yu Bi resumed tribute; Ying's title and enfeoffment were granted to him.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，毗上書獻方物，私假台使馮野夫西河太守，表求易林、式占、腰弩，文帝並與之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Bi submitted a memorial with local products, privately asking the court envoy Feng Yefu, Grand Administrator of Xihe, to request the Yilin, Shizhan, and crossbow-at-the-waist; Emperor Wen granted them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Bi sent a memorial with local goods and privately asked the court envoy Feng Yefu, grand administrator of Xihe, for the Yilin, Shizhan, and waist-mounted crossbow; Emperor Wen granted all.

sentences.zh: 毗死，子慶代立。

translations.literal: Bi died; his son Qing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Bi died and his son Qing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明元年，遣使求除授，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, envoys were sent requesting appointment and enfeoffment; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowu's first Daming year envoys asked for appointment; an edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 二年，慶遣上表，言行冠軍將軍、右賢王余紀十一人忠勤，並求顯進。

translations.literal: In the second year, Qing sent up a memorial stating that Acting Champion General and Right Worthy King Yu Ji and eleven others were loyal and diligent, all requesting promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Qing memorialized that Acting Champion General and Right Worthy King Yu Ji and eleven others were loyal and diligent and asked that they be advanced.

sentences.zh: 於是詔並加優進。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict advanced them all with favor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then advanced them all with favor.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始七年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, envoys were again sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming's seventh Taishi year envoys again brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 慶死，立子牟都。

translations.literal: Qing died; his son Moudu was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Qing died and Moudu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 都死，立子牟大。

translations.literal: Moudu died; his son Outai was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Moudu died and Outai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，除大都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In Yongming of Qi he was appointed Grand Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming he became Grand Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，進大號征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, his grand title was advanced to General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian one his grand title rose to General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 尋為高句麗所破，衰弱累年，遷居南韓地。

translations.literal: Soon he was broken by Koguryo; weakened for many years, they moved to settle in southern Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Koguryo broke them; weakened for years, they moved to southern Han lands.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，王餘隆始復遣使奉表，稱累破高麗，今始與通好，百濟更為強國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, King Yu Long first again sent envoys with a memorial, stating that having repeatedly broken Koguryo, they now first established friendly relations—and Baekje again became a powerful state.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong two King Yu Long sent envoys again, reporting repeated victories over Koguryo and a new opening of friendly ties—and Baekje grew strong once more.

sentences.zh: 其年，梁武帝詔隆為使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、甯東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Wu of Liang issued an edict making Long Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liang's Emperor Wu made Long Bearer of the Staff, commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 五年，隆死，詔復以其子明為持節、督百濟諸軍事、綏東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Long died; an edict had his son Ming succeed as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Assuages the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Long died; an edict made his son Ming Bearer of the Staff, commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Assuages the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 號所都城曰固麻，謂邑曰簷魯，如中國之言郡縣也。

translations.literal: They call their capital city Guma, and settlements Cheon-nok—like China's terms for commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital is called Guma and their towns Cheon-nok—like China's commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 其國土有二十二簷魯，皆以子弟宗族分據之。

translations.literal: The state has twenty-two cheon-nok, all held separately by sons, younger relatives, and clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has twenty-two cheon-nok, each held by sons, younger kin, and clansmen.

sentences.zh: 其人形長，衣服潔淨。

translations.literal: The people are tall in form; their clothes are clean.
translations.idiomatic: The people are tall and keep their dress clean.

sentences.zh: 其國近倭，頗有文身者。

translations.literal: Their country lies near Wa; many practice tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Their land lies near Wa; tattooing is common.

sentences.zh: 言語服章略與高麗同，呼帽曰冠，襦曰複衫，褲曰褌。

translations.literal: Speech and dress largely resemble Koguryo; they call a cap a guan, a jacket a fushan, trousers a kun.
translations.idiomatic: Speech and dress mostly match Koguryo; they call hats guan, jackets fushan, and trousers kun.

sentences.zh: 其言參諸夏，亦秦、韓之遺俗云。

translations.literal: Their speech partakes of the Central States—it is said to preserve customs of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Their language mixes with the Central States—said to preserve Qin and Han customs.

sentences.zh: 中大通六年、大同七年，累遣使獻方物，並請涅盤等經義、毛詩博士並工匠畫師等，並給之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongdatong and the seventh of Datong, envoys were repeatedly sent offering local products; they also requested masters of the Nirvana Sutra and other doctrinal texts, a Doctor of the Mao Odes, together with craftsmen and painters—and all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong six and Datong seven they sent envoys with local goods and asked for masters of the Nirvana Sutra and other scriptures, a Doctor of the Mao Odes, plus craftsmen and painters—all were granted.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing three envoys were sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 及至，見城闕荒毀，並號慟涕泣。

translations.literal: Once arrived, seeing the capital gates and towers in ruin, they all wailed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival, seeing ruined gates and walls, they wailed and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 侯景怒，囚執之，景平乃得還國。

translations.literal: Hou Jing grew angry and imprisoned them; only when Jing was pacified could they return home.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing in anger seized and held them; only after his defeat could they return home.

sentences.zh: 新羅，其先事詳北史，在百濟東南五千餘里。

translations.literal: Silla—the origin of its ruling house is given in detail in the Northern History; it lies over five thousand li southeast of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Silla's royal origins are treated fully in the Northern History; it lies more than five thousand li southeast of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 其地東濱大海，南北與句麗、百濟接。

translations.literal: Its territory fronts the great sea to the east; north and south it borders Koguryo and Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: It faces the eastern sea; north and south it touches Koguryo and Baekje.

sentences.zh: 魏時曰新盧；

translations.literal: Under Wei it was called Sin Lu;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei it was called Sin Lu;

sentences.zh: 宋時曰新羅，或曰斯羅。

translations.literal: under Song, Silla—or Sila.
translations.idiomatic: under Song, Silla—or Sila.

sentences.zh: 其國小，不能自通使聘。

translations.literal: The state is small and could not on its own dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was small and could not send envoys on its own.

sentences.zh: 梁普通二年，王姓募名泰，始使使隨百濟奉獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, King Mun named Tai first sent envoys following Baekje to offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong two King Mun named Tai first sent envoys with Baekje to present local goods.

sentences.zh: 其俗呼城曰健牟羅，其邑在內曰啄評，在外曰邑勒，亦中國之言郡縣也。

translations.literal: Their custom calls a city Geonmullara; settlements within are called chokpyeong, without are called eollok—again like China's commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: They call a city Geonmullara; inner towns are chokpyeong, outer ones eollok—again like China's commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 國有六啄評、五十二邑勒。

translations.literal: The state has six chokpyeong and fifty-two eollok.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has six chokpyeong and fifty-two eollok.

sentences.zh: 土地肥美，宜植五穀，多桑麻，作縑布，服牛乘馬，男女有別。

translations.literal: The land is rich and fair, suited for planting the five grains; mulberry and hemp are abundant and they make fine cloth; they use oxen for draft and horses for riding; men and women keep apart.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is rich and good for the five grains; mulberry and hemp abound for fine cloth; they draft with oxen, ride horses, and keep the sexes separate.

sentences.zh: 其官名有子賁旱支、壹旱支、齊旱支、謁旱支、壹吉支、奇貝旱支。

translations.literal: Their office titles include zibenhanzhi, yihanzhi, qihanzhi, yehanzhi, yijizhi, and qibeihanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Offices include zibenhanzhi, yihanzhi, qihanzhi, yehanzhi, yijizhi, and qibeihanzhi.

sentences.zh: 其冠曰遺子禮，襦曰尉解，褲曰柯半，靴曰洗。

translations.literal: Their crown is called yizili, their jacket wei-jie, their trousers ke-ban, their boots xi.
translations.idiomatic: They call the crown yizili, the jacket wei-jie, trousers ke-ban, and boots xi.

sentences.zh: 其拜及行與高麗相類。

translations.literal: Their bows and their gait resemble Koguryo.
translations.idiomatic: Their bows and gait match Koguryo.

sentences.zh: 無文字，刻木為信。

translations.literal: They have no writing; they carve wood for tokens of trust.
translations.idiomatic: Without writing, they carve wood for tokens.

sentences.zh: 語言待百濟而後通焉。

translations.literal: Their speech requires Baekje before it can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their language needs a Baekje interpreter.

sentences.zh: 倭國，其先所出及所在，事詳北史。

translations.literal: Wa—the origin of its ruling house and its location are given in detail in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Wa's royal origins and where it lies are treated fully in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 其官有伊支馬，次曰彌馬獲支，次曰奴往鞮。

translations.literal: Its offices include ikima, next mimakazhi, next nuchangti.
translations.idiomatic: Offices run ikima, then mimakazhi, then nuchangti.

sentences.zh: 人種禾、稻、紵、麻，蠶桑織績，有姜、桂、橘、椒、蘇。

translations.literal: The people plant millet, rice, ramie, and hemp; they raise silkworms and weave; they have ginger, cassia, oranges, pepper, and perilla.
translations.idiomatic: They grow grain, ramie, and hemp, raise silkworms and weave, and have ginger, cassia, oranges, pepper, and perilla.

sentences.zh: 出黑雉、真珠、青玉。

translations.literal: They produce black pheasants, pearls, and green jade.
translations.idiomatic: Black pheasants, pearls, and green jade come from the land.

sentences.zh: 有獸如牛名山鼠，又有大蛇吞此獸。

translations.literal: There is a beast like an ox called the mountain rat; there is also a great serpent that swallows this beast.
translations.idiomatic: A beast like an ox, called the mountain rat, lives there—and a great serpent that devours it.

sentences.zh: 蛇皮堅不可斫，其上有孔，乍開乍閉，時或有光，射中而蛇則死矣。

translations.literal: The serpent's hide is hard and cannot be cut; on it are holes that now open, now close; at times light shines from them—shoot through one and the serpent dies.
translations.idiomatic: Its hide is uncuttable, pierced with holes that open and shut and sometimes shine; a shot through a hole kills the serpent.

sentences.zh: 物產略與儋耳、朱崖同。

translations.literal: Products are roughly the same as Dan'er and Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: Local products resemble Dan'er and Zhuya.

sentences.zh: 地氣溫暖，風俗不淫。

translations.literal: The land is warm; custom is not licentious.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild and morals restrained.

sentences.zh: 男女皆露髫，富貴者以錦繡雜采為帽，似中國胡公頭。

translations.literal: Men and women all wear their hair loose; the wealthy make caps of brocade and mixed colors, resembling the Hu gong head of China.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wear loose hair; the wealthy wear brocade caps like the Hu gong head of China.

sentences.zh: 食飲用籩豆。

translations.literal: For food and drink they use platters and bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Meals are served on platters and in bowls.

sentences.zh: 其死有棺無槨，封土作塚。

translations.literal: At death there is a coffin but no outer shell; earth is piled to make the mound.
translations.idiomatic: The dead receive a coffin without an outer shell, and earth is heaped for the tomb.

sentences.zh: 人性皆嗜酒。

translations.literal: By nature the people all love wine.
translations.idiomatic: The people are fond of wine.

sentences.zh: 俗不知正歲，多壽考，或至八九十，或至百歲。

translations.literal: Custom does not know the proper New Year; many live long, often reaching eighty or ninety, sometimes a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no proper calendar year; many live to eighty or ninety, some to a hundred.

sentences.zh: 其俗女多男少，貴者至四五妻，賤者猶至兩三妻。

translations.literal: Custom has more women than men; the noble may have four or five wives, the lowly still two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumber men; nobles take four or five wives, commoners two or three.

sentences.zh: 婦人不媱妒，無盜竊，少諍訟。

translations.literal: Wives feel no jealous rage; there is no theft; lawsuits are few.
translations.idiomatic: Wives do not grow jealous; theft is rare and lawsuits few.

sentences.zh: 若犯法，輕者沒其妻子，重則滅其宗族。

translations.literal: If one breaks the law, the lighter penalty enslaves wife and children; the heavier exterminates the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: Light crimes cost wife and children; grave ones wipe out the clan.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝時，有倭王贊遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the time of Jin Emperor An, King Zan of Wa sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Emperor An, Wa King Zan sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 及宋武帝永初二年，詔曰：「倭贊遠誠宜甄，可賜除授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu of Song, an edict said: "Zan of Wa has shown devotion from afar and should be distinguished—let rank and appointment be granted."
translations.idiomatic: In Song Wu's second Yongchu year an edict read, "Wa's Zan has shown true devotion from afar—let rank and appointment be granted."

sentences.zh: 」文帝元嘉二年，贊又遣司馬曹達奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, Zan again sent Marshal Cao Da with a memorial presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Wen's second Yuanjia year Zan again sent Marshal Cao Da with a memorial and local goods.

sentences.zh: 贊死，弟珍立，遣使貢獻，自稱使持節、都督倭百濟新羅任那秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭國王，表求除正。

translations.literal: When Zan died, his younger brother Chen succeeded and sent envoys with tribute, styling himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Qin Han, and Mo Han six states, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa, and requesting formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zan died and his brother Chen succeeded, sent tribute, and styled himself Bearer of the Staff, commander of Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Qin Han, and Mo Han, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa, asking for formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 詔除安東將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: An edict made him General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 珍又求除正倭洧等十三人平西、征虜、冠軍、輔國將軍等號，詔並聽之。

translations.literal: Chen again requested formal appointment for thirteen men including You of Wa and others as Generals Who Pacify the West, Campaign Against the Barbarians, Champion, and Assist the State; an edict granted all.
translations.idiomatic: Chen again asked formal ranks for thirteen men including You of Wa and others as Generals Who Pacify the West, Campaign Against the Barbarians, Champion, and Assist the State; an edict granted all.

sentences.zh: 二十年，倭國王濟遣使奉獻，復以為安東將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, King Ji of Wa sent envoys with tribute and was again made General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Wa King Ji sent tribute and was again made General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，加使持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事，安東將軍如故；

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was made Bearer of the Staff and Commander of all military affairs of Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qin Han, and Mo Han six states, General Who Pacifies the East as before;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he gained the staff and command over Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qin Han, and Mo Han, with General Who Pacifies the East unchanged;

sentences.zh: 並除所上二十三人職。

translations.literal: and the twenty-three offices he submitted were all granted.
translations.idiomatic: and the twenty-three offices he submitted were all granted.

sentences.zh: 濟死，世子興遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: When Ji died, the heir Xing sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ji died and the heir Xing sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明六年，詔授興安東將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, an edict appointed Xing General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowu's sixth Daming year an edict made Xing General Who Pacifies the East and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 興死，弟武立，自稱使持節、都督倭百濟新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓七國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭國王。

translations.literal: When Xing died, his younger brother Wu succeeded, styling himself Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Wa, Baekje, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qin Han, and Mo Han seven states, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Xing died and his brother Wu succeeded, styling himself Bearer of the Staff, commander of seven states, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明二年，遣使上表，言：「自昔祖禰，躬擐甲胄，跋涉山川，不遑寧處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, envoys were sent with a memorial stating: "From former ancestors and fathers, we ourselves donned armor, traversed mountains and rivers, and had no leisure to rest."
translations.idiomatic: In Shun's second Shengming year envoys sent a memorial: "From our ancestors we donned armor, crossed mountains and rivers, and knew no rest."

sentences.zh: 東征毛人五十五國，西服眾夷六十六國，陵平海北九十五國。

translations.literal: We campaigned east against the hairy people of fifty-five states, west subdued the many Yi of sixty-six states, and overawed ninety-five states north of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: We campaigned east against fifty-five hairy peoples' states, west subdued sixty-six Yi states, and overawed ninety-five states north of the sea.

sentences.zh: 王道融泰，廓土遐畿，累葉朝宗，不愆於歲。

translations.literal: The royal way was harmonious and secure, the frontier lands were cleared, and generation after generation paid court tribute without missing a year.
translations.idiomatic: The royal way was secure, frontiers cleared, and tribute came year after year without fail.

sentences.zh: 道徑百濟，裝飾船舫，而句麗無道，圖欲見吞。

translations.literal: The route passes through Baekje, where ships are fitted out, while Koguryo is lawless and seeks to swallow us.
translations.idiomatic: The route runs through Baekje where ships are fitted out, while lawless Koguryo seeks to swallow us.

sentences.zh: 臣亡考濟方欲大舉，奄喪父兄，使垂成之功，不獲一簣。

translations.literal: My late father Ji was about to launch a great campaign when he suddenly lost father and elder brothers, so the work nearly complete could not gain even one basketful more.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Ji was about to launch a great campaign when he suddenly lost father and brothers, and the nearly finished work lost its final basketful.

sentences.zh: 今欲練兵申父兄之志，竊自假開府儀同三司，其餘咸各假授，以勸忠節」。

translations.literal: Now I wish to drill troops to carry out my father and brothers' intent, and I venture to request for myself an acting Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; the rest I likewise request by acting appointment, to encourage loyal service."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to drill troops to fulfill my father and brothers' intent and venture to request an acting Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office; the rest I likewise request by acting appointment to encourage loyal service."

sentences.zh: 詔除武使持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭王。

translations.literal: An edict made Wu Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qin Han, and Mo Han six states, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Wu Bearer of the Staff, commander of six states, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Wa.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，除武持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan of Qi he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Qin Han, and Mo Han six states, and General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianyuan he became Bearer of the Staff, commander of six states, and General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝即位，進武號征東大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu ascended, Wu's title rose to General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 其南有侏儒國，人長四尺。

translations.literal: South of them is the Dwarf Country; the people are four feet tall.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lies the Dwarf Country, whose people stand four feet tall.

sentences.zh: 又南有黑齒國、裸國，去倭四千餘里，船行可一年至。

translations.literal: Farther south are the Black-Tooth Country and the Naked Country, more than four thousand li from Wa—a year's voyage by ship.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lie Black-Tooth and Naked countries, four thousand li from Wa and a year's sail away.

sentences.zh: 又西南萬里有海人，身黑眼白，裸而醜，其肉美，行者或射而食之。

translations.literal: Still farther southwest, ten thousand li off, are sea people—black of body, white of eye, naked and ugly; their flesh is savory; travelers sometimes shoot and eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li southwest live sea people, black-skinned and white-eyed, naked and foul; travelers find their flesh savory and sometimes shoot them for food.

sentences.zh: 文身國在倭東北七千餘里，人體有文如獸，其額上有三文，文直者貴，文小者賤。

translations.literal: The Tattooed Country lies more than seven thousand li northeast of Wa; people's bodies bear marks like beasts; on the forehead are three marks—straight marks mean nobility, small marks mean baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed Country stands seven thousand li northeast of Wa; bodies are tattooed like beasts, with three forehead marks—straight for noble, small for low.

sentences.zh: 土俗歡樂，物豐而賤，行客不齎糧。

translations.literal: Local custom is joyous; goods are plentiful and cheap; travelers need not carry provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Life is merry, goods cheap and abundant; travelers carry no rations.

sentences.zh: 有屋宇，無城郭。

translations.literal: They have houses but no walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: They build houses without city walls.

sentences.zh: 國王所居，飾以金銀珍麗，繞屋為塹，廣一丈，實以水銀，雨則流于水銀之上。

translations.literal: Where the king dwells is adorned with gold, silver, and rare splendor; around the house runs a moat one zhang wide, filled with mercury; when it rains the water flows atop the mercury.
translations.idiomatic: The king's residence gleams with gold, silver, and rare finery; a one-zhang moat rings the house, filled with mercury; rain runs over the mercury's surface.

sentences.zh: 市用珍寶。

translations.literal: The market uses precious gems.
translations.idiomatic: Markets trade in precious gems.

sentences.zh: 犯輕罪者則鞭杖，犯死罪則置猛獸食之，有枉則獸避而不食，經宿則赦之。

translations.literal: Light crimes are punished with the whip and staff; capital crimes are punished by setting fierce beasts to devour the offender—if there is injustice the beasts avoid and will not eat; after one night he is pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Light offenses bring the whip and staff; capital crimes are judged by fierce beasts—if the man is wronged the beasts refuse him; after a night he goes free.

sentences.zh: 大漢國在文身國東五千餘里，無兵戈，不攻戰，風俗並與文身國同而言語異。

translations.literal: The Great Han Country lies more than five thousand li east of the Tattooed Country; it has no weapons of war and does not make battle; custom is the same as the Tattooed Country, but the language differs.
translations.idiomatic: Great Han Country lies five thousand li east of Tattooed Country; it keeps no arms and makes no war; custom matches Tattooed Country but speech differs.

sentences.zh: 扶桑國

translations.literal: Fusang Country
translations.idiomatic: Fusang Country

sentences.zh: 扶桑國者，齊永元元年，其國有沙門慧深來至荊州，說云：「扶桑在大漢國東二萬餘里，地在中國之東。

translations.literal: Fusang Country—in the first year of Qi Yongyuan a monk of that land, Hui Shen, came to Jing Province and said: "Fusang lies more than twenty thousand li east of the Great Han Country, its land east of China;
translations.idiomatic: Fusang—in Qi Yongyuan 1 the monk Hui Shen reached Jing Province and reported, "Fusang lies twenty thousand li east of Great Han, east of China;

sentences.zh: 其土多扶桑木，故以為名。

translations.literal: the soil has much fusang wood, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: fusang trees abound, giving the land its name.

sentences.zh: 扶桑葉似桐，初生如筍，國人食之。

translations.literal: Fusang leaves resemble paulownia and when first sprouting are like bamboo shoots; the people eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Fusang leaves resemble paulownia, new shoots like bamboo; the people eat them.

sentences.zh: 實如梨而赤，績其皮為布，以為衣，亦以為錦。

translations.literal: The fruit is like a pear and red; they spin the bark into cloth for clothing, also using it as brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit is red like pears; bark is spun into cloth for dress and brocade.

sentences.zh: 作板屋，無城郭。

translations.literal: They build plank houses and have no walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: They live in plank houses without walled cities.

sentences.zh: 有文字，以扶桑皮為紙。

translations.literal: They have writing and use fusang bark for paper.
translations.idiomatic: They write on paper made from fusang bark.

sentences.zh: 無兵甲，不攻戰。

translations.literal: They have no armor or weapons and do not make battle.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no armor or arms and make no war.

sentences.zh: 其國法有南北獄，若有犯，輕罪者入南獄，重罪者入北獄。

translations.literal: By the law of the state there are southern and northern prisons; if someone commits a crime, light offenders enter the southern prison, grave offenders the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: State law divides prisons into south and north; light crimes go to the south prison, grave crimes to the north.

sentences.zh: 有赦則放南獄，不赦北獄。

translations.literal: When there is an amnesty the southern prison is pardoned; the northern prison is not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties free the south prison, never the north.

sentences.zh: 在北獄者男女相配，生男八歲為奴，生女九歲為婢。

translations.literal: Those in the northern prison are paired man and woman; a boy at eight becomes a slave, a girl at nine a maid.
translations.idiomatic: Northern prisoners are paired; boys become slaves at eight, girls maids at nine.

sentences.zh: 犯罪之身，至死不出。

translations.literal: The bodies of the condemned never leave until death.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned bodies never leave until death.

sentences.zh: 貴人有罪，國人大會，坐罪人于坑，對之宴飲分訣若死別焉。

translations.literal: When a noble commits a crime the state holds a great assembly, seating the guilty in a pit while feasting opposite him—parting words as at a final farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When nobles sin the realm feasts above a pit where the condemned sit, taking leave as at death.

sentences.zh: 以灰繞之，其一重則一身摒退，二重則及子孫，三重者則及七世。

translations.literal: Ash is piled around them; one layer of ash removes one person from the company, two layers reach sons and grandsons, three layers reach seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ash rings the pit—one layer dismisses the offender, two reach sons and grandsons, three reach seven generations.

sentences.zh: 名國王為乙祁。

translations.literal: The king is called yiji.
translations.idiomatic: They call the king yiji.

sentences.zh: 貴人第一者為對盧，第二者為小對盧，第三者為納咄沙。

translations.literal: The first-rank noble is called duilu, the second lesser duilu, the third nazuo-sha.
translations.idiomatic: First nobles are duilu, second lesser duilu, third nazuo-sha.

sentences.zh: 國王行有鼓角導從。

translations.literal: When the king travels drums and horns lead the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The king travels to drum and horn.

sentences.zh: 其衣色隨年改易，甲乙年青，丙丁年赤，戊己年黃，庚辛年白，壬癸年黑。

translations.literal: Garment colors change with the year—green in jia and yi years, red in bing and ding, yellow in wu and ji, white in geng and xin, black in ren and gui.
translations.idiomatic: Dress color follows the year—green for jia-yi, red for bing-ding, yellow for wu-ji, white for geng-xin, black for ren-gui.

sentences.zh: 有牛角甚長，以角載物，至勝二十斛。

translations.literal: Ox horns are very long and used to carry goods, bearing up to twenty hu.
translations.idiomatic: Long ox horns serve as load-bearers, holding twenty hu.

sentences.zh: 有馬車、牛車、鹿車。

translations.literal: There are horse-carts, ox-carts, and deer-carts.
translations.idiomatic: They use horse-carts, ox-carts, and deer-carts.

sentences.zh: 國人養鹿如中國畜牛，以乳為酪。

translations.literal: The people raise deer as China raises cattle, making curds from the milk.
translations.idiomatic: They herd deer as China herds cattle and make curds from the milk.

sentences.zh: 有赤梨，經年不壞。

translations.literal: They have red pears that keep for years without spoiling.
translations.idiomatic: Red pears keep for years.

sentences.zh: 多蒲桃。

translations.literal: Grapes are plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Grapes abound.

sentences.zh: 其地無鐵有銅，不貴金銀。

translations.literal: The land has no iron but has copper; gold and silver are not prized.
translations.idiomatic: Iron is absent, copper present; gold and silver are cheap.

sentences.zh: 市無租估。

translations.literal: Markets levy no tolls or appraisals.
translations.idiomatic: Markets take no toll or appraisal fee.

sentences.zh: 其昏姻法，則婿往女家門外作屋，晨夕灑掃，經年而女不悅即驅之，相悅乃成昏。

translations.literal: In marriage the bridegroom builds a house outside the bride's family gate, sweeping morning and evening; if after a year the girl is not pleased she drives him off—only when both are pleased do they marry.
translations.idiomatic: The groom builds a hut outside the bride's gate and sweeps it daily; if she is displeased after a year she sends him away—marriage comes only by mutual consent.

sentences.zh: 昏禮大抵與中國同。

translations.literal: Marriage rites are largely the same as China's.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage rites mostly match China's.

sentences.zh: 親喪七日不食，祖父母喪五日不食，兄弟伯叔姑姊妹三日不食。

translations.literal: For a parent's death one does not eat for seven days; for grandparents' death five days; for brothers, uncles, aunts, and sisters three days.
translations.idiomatic: Parents' mourning brings seven days without food, grandparents' five, brothers and uncles three.

sentences.zh: 設座為神像，朝夕拜奠，不制衰絰。

translations.literal: They set up a seat as an image of the spirit, bowing morning and evening, and do not make hemp mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: They set a spirit seat and bow morning and evening without hemp mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 嗣王立，三年不親國事。

translations.literal: When the heir succeeds to the throne, for three years he does not attend to state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A new king leaves state affairs untouched for three years.

sentences.zh: 其俗舊無佛法。

translations.literal: Their custom formerly had no Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: They once had no Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 宋大明二年，罽賓國嘗有比丘五人遊行其國，流通佛法經像，教令出家，風俗遂改。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming under Song, five monks of Kapisa once traveled their country, circulating Buddhist scriptures and images and teaching people to leave the household; custom thereupon changed."
translations.idiomatic: In Song's second Daming year five Kapisa monks traveled the land, spreading Buddhist scriptures and images and teaching ordination, and custom changed."

sentences.zh: 慧深又云：「扶桑東千餘里有女國，容貌端正，色甚潔白，身體有毛，發長委地。

translations.literal: Huishen also said: "More than a thousand li east of Fusang is a land of women; their features are proper, their color very pure white, their bodies have hair, and their hair trails to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Huishen also said that east of Fusang, a thousand li and more away, lay a realm of women—handsome of face, very fair in complexion, hairy of body, with hair that spilled to the ground.

sentences.zh: 至二三月競入水則任娠，六七月產子。

translations.literal: When the second and third months come, they rush into the water and become pregnant; in the sixth or seventh month they bear children.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third months they all plunge into the water and conceive; by the sixth or seventh month they give birth.

sentences.zh: 女人胸前無乳，項後生毛，根白，毛中有汁以乳子。

translations.literal: The women have no breasts on their chests; hair grows behind the nape, white at the root, and the hair contains sap with which they nurse their children.
translations.idiomatic: Women have no breasts on the chest; behind the neck grows hair, white at the root, and sap within the hair feeds the child.

sentences.zh: 百日能行，三四年則成人矣。

translations.literal: At a hundred days the child can walk; in three or four years it reaches adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: At a hundred days the child can walk; in three or four years it is grown.

sentences.zh: 見人驚避，偏畏丈夫。

translations.literal: They startle and flee at the sight of people, and especially fear men.
translations.idiomatic: They startle at the sight of people and flee, and fear men above all.

sentences.zh: 食鹹草如禽獸。

translations.literal: They eat salt-grass like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: They eat salt-grass as birds and beasts do.

sentences.zh: 鹹草葉似邪蒿，而氣香味鹹。

translations.literal: Salt-grass leaves resemble wormwood, but its fragrance is salty.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-grass leaves resemble wormwood, yet its scent is salty and fragrant.

sentences.zh: 梁天監六年，有晉安人度海，為風所飄至一島，登岸，有人居止，女則如中國，而言語不可曉。

translations.literal: In Tianjian 6, a man of Jin'an crossed the sea and was blown by wind to an island; landing ashore, he found people dwelling there; the women were like those of China, but their speech could not be understood.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 6 a man of Jin'an crossed the sea, was blown by wind to an island, went ashore, and found people living there; the women resembled Chinese women, but their speech could not be understood.

sentences.zh: 男則人身而狗頭，其聲如吠。

translations.literal: The men had human bodies and dogs' heads, their voices like barking.
translations.idiomatic: The men had human bodies and dogs' heads, and barked when they spoke.

sentences.zh: 其食有小豆，其衣如布。

translations.literal: Their food included small beans; their clothes were like cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They ate small beans and wore cloth-like garments.

sentences.zh: 築土為牆，其形圓，其戶如竇云。」

translations.literal: They built walls of earth in a round shape, and their doors were like burrows."
translations.idiomatic: They built round earthen walls, and their doors were like burrows."

sentences.zh: 河南、宕昌、鄧至、武興，其本並為氐、羌之地。

translations.literal: Henan, Dangchang, Dengzhi, and Wuxing—all were originally Di and Qiang lands.
translations.idiomatic: Henan, Dangchang, Dengzhi, and Wuxing were all originally Di and Qiang territory.

sentences.zh: 自晉南遷，九州分裂，此等諸國，地分西垂，提挈于魏，時通江左。

translations.literal: After Jin moved south, the Nine Provinces split apart; these various states lay along the western marches, were drawn along by Wei, and from time to time communicated with the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin moved south and the Nine Provinces split, these states lay on the western frontier, were drawn along by Wei, and from time to time communicated with the south.

sentences.zh: 今采其舊土，編於西戎云。

translations.literal: Now we gather their former territories and compile them under the Western Rong, as follows.
translations.idiomatic: Here we gather their former domains and record them among the Western Rong tribes.

sentences.zh: 河南國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Henan
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Henan

sentences.zh: 河南王者，其先出自鮮卑慕容氏。

translations.literal: The kings of Henan originally came from the Xianbei Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Henan traced their line to the Xianbei Murong clan.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容弈洛幹有二子，庶長曰吐谷渾，嫡曰廆洛幹。

translations.literal: At the start, Murong Yiluoqian had two sons—the elder by a concubine was called Tuyuhun, the heir was called Hui Luogan.
translations.idiomatic: At first Murong Yiluoqian had two sons: the elder by a concubine was Tuyuhun; the heir was Hui Luogan.

sentences.zh: 卒，廆嗣位，吐谷渾避之，西徙上隴，度枹罕，出涼州西南，至赤水而居之。

translations.literal: When he died, Hui succeeded; Tuyuhun avoided him, migrated west to Upper Long, crossed Fuhan, passed southwest of Liangzhou, and settled at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Hui took the throne. Tuyuhun fled west, moving up onto Long, crossing Fuhan, passing southwest of Liangzhou, and settling at Chishui.

sentences.zh: 地在河南，故以為號。

translations.literal: The land lay south of the river, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lay south of the river—hence the name Henan.

sentences.zh: 事詳北史。

translations.literal: The matter is given in detail in the Book of Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: For the full account, see the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 其界東至疊川，西鄰于闐，北接高昌，東北通秦嶺，方千餘里，蓋古之流沙地焉。

translations.literal: Its borders reached Diechuan in the east, adjoined Yutian in the west, connected with Gaochang in the north, and linked to the Qin Mountains in the northeast—over a thousand li square, largely the ancient land of shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders ran east to Diechuan, west to Yutian, north to Gaochang, and northeast to the Qin Mountains—over a thousand li on a side, largely the old land of shifting sands.

sentences.zh: 乏草木，少水潦，四時恒有冰雪，唯六七月雨雹甚盛。

translations.literal: It lacked grass and trees, had little rain and flood; ice and snow persisted through the four seasons—only in the sixth and seventh months hail and rain were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees were scarce, rain and flood rare; ice and snow held through the four seasons—only in the sixth and seventh months did hail and rain fall heavily.

sentences.zh: 若晴則風飄沙礫，常蔽光景。

translations.literal: When skies cleared, wind blew sand and gravel, often blotting out the light.
translations.idiomatic: When skies cleared, wind whipped sand and gravel and often blotted out the light.

sentences.zh: 其地有麥無穀。

translations.literal: The land had wheat but no millet.
translations.idiomatic: The land grew wheat but not millet.

sentences.zh: 有青海方數百里，放牝馬其側，輒生駒，土人謂之龍種，故其國多善馬。

translations.literal: There was Qinghai Sea, several hundred li square—mares pastured beside it would bear foals; locals called them dragon stock, so the state had many fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Sea spread several hundred li across; mares pastured beside it would foal, and locals called the offspring dragon stock—hence the realm's many fine horses.

sentences.zh: 有屋宇，雜以百子帳，即穹廬也。

translations.literal: They had houses, mixed with hundred-son tents—that is, yurt tents.
translations.idiomatic: They had houses mixed with hundred-son tents—that is, felt yurts.

sentences.zh: 著小袖袍，小口褲，大頭長裙帽。

translations.literal: They wore small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and large-headed long-skirt caps.
translations.idiomatic: They wore small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and large-headed caps with long skirts.

sentences.zh: 女子被髮為辮。

translations.literal: Women wore their hair loose in braids.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore their hair loose and braided.

sentences.zh: 其後吐谷渾孫葉延，頗識書記，自謂曾祖弈洛幹始封昌黎公，吾蓋公孫之子也。

translations.literal: Later Tuyuhun's grandson Yeyan knew books and records well; he said his great-grandfather Yiluoqian was first enfeoffed as Duke of Changli—"I am the duke's grandson's son."
translations.idiomatic: Later Tuyuhun's grandson Yeyan was well versed in writing; he said his great-grandfather Yiluoqian was first enfeoffed Duke of Changli—"I am the duke's grandson's son."

sentences.zh: 禮以王父字為氏，因姓吐谷渾，亦為國號。

translations.literal: By ritual one takes the paternal grandfather's name as the clan name—thus they surnamed Tuyuhun, which also became the state name.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual the paternal grandfather's name becomes the clan name; they therefore took Tuyuhun as surname and as the name of the state.

sentences.zh: 至其末孫阿豺，始通江左，受官爵。

translations.literal: Down to his last descendant Achen, they first opened relations with the lands south of the Yangzi and received Chinese office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the last descendant Achen did they first deal with the Jiangzuo court and receive Chinese offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 弟子慕延，宋元嘉末，又自號河南王。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Muyan, at the end of Song Yuanjia, again styled himself King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Muyan, at the end of Song Yuanjia, again styled himself King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 慕延死，從弟拾寅立，乃用書契，起城池，築宮殿。

translations.literal: When Muyan died, his cousin Shibin succeeded; then they used written records, raised walls and cities, and built palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Muyan died, his cousin Shibin succeeded. Then they used written records, raised walls and cities, and built palaces.

sentences.zh: 其小王並立宅國中。

translations.literal: Lesser kings all built residences within the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser kings all built houses of their own within the realm.

sentences.zh: 有佛法。

translations.literal: There was Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was present.

sentences.zh: 拾寅死，子度易侯立。

translations.literal: When Shibin died, his son Duyihou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shibin died, his son Duyihou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 易侯死，子休留代立。

translations.literal: When Duyihou died, his son Xiuliudai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Duyihou died, his son Xiuliudai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，以代為使持節、都督西秦河沙三州、鎮西將軍、護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, Xiuliudai was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of West Qin, He, and Sha commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of West Qin and He.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming, Xiuliudai was made bearer of the staff, area commander of West Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Qiang, and inspector of West Qin and He.

sentences.zh: 宕昌國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Dangchang
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Dangchang

sentences.zh: 宕昌國，在河南國之東、益州之西北隴西之地，西羌種也。

translations.literal: Dangchang lay east of the Kingdom of Henan, in the Longxi region northwest of Yizhou—a Western Qiang people.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang stood east of Henan, in the Longxi country northwest of Yizhou—a Western Qiang people.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，其王梁瑾忽始獻方物。

translations.literal: In Song Emperor Xiaowu's reign, its king Liang Jinhu first presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Emperor Xiaowu, King Liang Jinhu first sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 梁天監四年，王梁彌博來獻甘草、當歸。

translations.literal: In Liang Tianjian 4, King Liang Mibo came presenting licorice and angelica.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 4, King Liang Mibo brought licorice and angelica.

sentences.zh: 詔以為使持節、都督河涼二州諸軍事、安西將軍、東羌校尉、河涼二州刺史、隴西公、宕昌王。

translations.literal: An edict made him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of military affairs of He and Liang provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Governor of He and Liang provinces, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne made him bearer of the staff, area commander of He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, governor of both provinces, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 佩以金章。

translations.literal: He was invested with a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: He received a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 彌博死，子彌泰立。

translations.literal: When Mibo died, his son Mitai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mibo died, his son Mitai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，復策授以父爵位。

translations.literal: In Datong 7, his father's titles were again granted by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 an edict restored his father's titles.

sentences.zh: 其衣服風俗與河南略同。

translations.literal: Their dress and customs broadly match Henan's.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing and customs closely resembled Henan's.

sentences.zh: 鄧至國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Dengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Dengzhi

sentences.zh: 武興國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Wuxing
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Wuxing

sentences.zh: 武興國，本仇池。

translations.literal: Wuxing was originally Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing had originally been Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 楊難當自立為秦王，宋文帝遣裴方明討之，難當奔魏。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang set himself up as King of Qin; Song Emperor Wen sent Pei Fangming against him; Nandang fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang declared himself King of Qin; Song Emperor Wen sent Pei Fangming to suppress him, and Nandang fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 其兄子文德又聚眾葭蘆，宋因授以爵位。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Wendé gathered forces at Jialu; Song therefore granted him titles.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wendé rallied men at Jialu; Song enfeoffed him.

sentences.zh: 魏又攻之，文德奔漢中。

translations.literal: Wei attacked again and Wendé fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked again and Wendé fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從弟僧嗣又自立，復戍葭蘆，卒。

translations.literal: His younger clansman Wensie set himself up, again garrisoned Jialu, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wensie then declared himself ruler, reoccupied Jialu, and died.

sentences.zh: 文德弟文度立，以弟文弘為白水太守，屯武興。

translations.literal: Wendé's younger brother Wendu succeeded; he made his younger brother Wen Hong prefect of Baishui and encamped at Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wendé's brother Wendu took over, made Wen Hong prefect of Baishui, and encamped at Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 宋世以為武都王。

translations.literal: Under Song he was titled King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Song titled him King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 武興之國自於此矣。

translations.literal: The state of Wuxing dates from this.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Wuxing began here.

sentences.zh: 難當族弟廣香又攻殺文度，自立為陰平王、葭蘆鎮主。

translations.literal: Nandang's clansman Guangxiang attacked and killed Wendu, set himself up as King of Yinping and commandant of the Jialu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's kinsman Guangxiang killed Wendu and made himself King of Yinping and commandant of Jialu.

sentences.zh: 死，子炅立。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Jiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Jiong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 炅死，子崇祖立。

translations.literal: When Jiong died, his son Chongzu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong died, his son Chongzu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 崇祖死，子孟孫立。

translations.literal: When Chongzu died, his son Mengersun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzu died, his son Mengersun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，魏南梁州刺史仇池公楊靈珍據泥功山歸齊，齊武帝以靈珍為北梁州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, Wei's Southern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi Yang Lingzhen held Migong Mountain and submitted to Qi; Emperor Wu of Qi made Lingzhen Northern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming, Yang Lingzhen—Wei's southern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi—held Migong Mountain and submitted; Emperor Wu of Qi made him northern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 文洪死，以族人集始為北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: When Wen Hong died, clansman Jishi was made Northern Qinzhou inspector and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Hong died, the clansman Jishi became northern Qinzhou inspector and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，以集始為持節、都督秦雍二州諸軍事、輔國將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: At the start of Liang Tianjian, Jishi was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Qin and Yong military affairs, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Northern Qinzhou inspector, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, Jishi became bearer of the staff, area commander of Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, northern Qinzhou inspector, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 靈珍為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Lingzhen was made Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen became champion general.

sentences.zh: 孟孫為假節、督沙州諸軍事、平羌校尉、沙州刺史、陰平王。

translations.literal: Mengersun was made Acting Staff, Commander of Shazhou military affairs, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Mengersun became acting staff, commander of Shazhou, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, inspector of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 集始死，子紹先襲爵位。

translations.literal: When Jishi died, his son Shaoxian inherited the titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Jishi died, his son Shaoxian inherited the titles.

sentences.zh: 二年，以靈珍為持節、督隴右諸軍事、左將軍、北涼州刺史、仇池王。

translations.literal: In year 2, Lingzhen was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Longyou military affairs, Left General, Northern Liangzhou inspector, and King of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Lingzhen became bearer of the staff, commander of Longyou, left general, northern Liangzhou inspector, and King of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 十年，孟孫死，詔贈安沙將軍、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 10, Mengersun died; an edict posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Sands and Northern Yongzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Mengersun died; the throne posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the Sands and northern Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 子定襲封爵。

translations.literal: His son Ding inherited the enfeoffment and titles.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding inherited the fief and titles.

sentences.zh: 紹先死，子智慧立。

translations.literal: When Shaoxian died, his son Zhihui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoxian died, his son Zhihui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大同元年，克復漢中，智慧遣使上表，求率四千戶歸梁，詔許焉，即以為東益州。

translations.literal: In Datong 1, Hanzhong was recovered; Zhihui sent envoys with a memorial asking to lead four thousand households back to Liang; an edict permitted it, and the area was made Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1, after Hanzhong was retaken, Zhihui asked by memorial to bring four thousand households to Liang; the throne agreed and made the region Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其國東連秦嶺，西接宕昌。

translations.literal: Its state adjoined the Qin Mountains to the east and Dangchang to the west.
translations.idiomatic: It touched the Qin Mountains on the east and Dangchang on the west.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有苻氏、姜氏、梁氏。

translations.literal: Great surnames include Fu, Jiang, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Leading clans were Fu, Jiang, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 言語與中國同。

translations.literal: Their speech matches China's.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke the same language as China.

sentences.zh: 著烏皁突騎帽，長身小袖袍，小口褲，皮褲。

translations.literal: They wear black-felt chieftain's riding caps, long-bodied small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and leather trousers.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black felt riding caps, long tight-sleeved coats, narrow trousers, and leather leggings.

sentences.zh: 地植九穀。

translations.literal: The land grows the nine grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded the nine grains.

sentences.zh: 婚姻備六禮。

translations.literal: Marriage observes all six rites.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage followed the full six rites.

sentences.zh: 知書疏。

translations.literal: They know letters and documents.
translations.idiomatic: They were literate in correspondence.

sentences.zh: 種桑麻。

translations.literal: They plant mulberry and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: They cultivated mulberry and hemp.

sentences.zh: 出紬絹布漆蠟椒等，山出銅鐵。

translations.literal: They produce pongee, silk, cloth, lacquer, wax, pepper, and the like; their mountains yield copper and iron.
translations.idiomatic: They exported pongee, silk, cloth, lacquer, wax, pepper, and similar goods; the mountains produced copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 書云「蠻夷猾夏」，其作梗也已舊。

translations.literal: The Documents say, "The Man and Yi harass Xia," and their obstruction is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents warn that "barbarians harass the heartland," and their defiance is an old story.

sentences.zh: 及于宋之方盛，蓋亦屢興戍役，豈詩所謂「蠢爾蠻荊，大邦為讎。

translations.literal: When Song was at its height, garrison labor was raised again and again—is this not what the Odes mean by "Stupid are you, southern barbarians of Jing—the great state becomes your foe.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's heyday the court raised garrison after garrison—was this not the Odes' warning: "Stupid are you, southern barbarians of Jing—the great state becomes your foe.

sentences.zh: 」者乎。

translations.literal: "—is this not so?
translations.idiomatic: "—was it not so?

sentences.zh: 今亦編錄以備諸蠻云爾。

translations.literal: Now they too are compiled here to complete the record of the various Man.
translations.idiomatic: They are recorded here as well, to complete the roster of the Man peoples.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍州蠻，盤瓠之後也，種落布在諸郡縣。

translations.literal: The Man of Jing and Yong provinces were descendants of Panhu; their tribes were scattered through the various commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Man of Jing and Yong were descended from Panhu, their clans spread through commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 宋時因晉于荊州置南蠻、雍州置甯蠻校尉以領之。

translations.literal: Under Song, following Jin, Southern Man was established in Jingzhou and the Colonel Who Pacifies the Man in Yongzhou to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: Song, following Jin, placed a Southern Man office in Jingzhou and a Pacifying-Man colonel in Yongzhou to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，罷南蠻並大府，而寧蠻如故。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Southern Man was abolished and merged into the great prefecture, while the Pacifying-Man office remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Southern Man was abolished and folded into the great prefecture; the Pacifying-Man office remained.

sentences.zh: 蠻之順附者，一戶輸穀數斛，其餘無雜調。

translations.literal: Man who submitted paid several hu of grain per household; beyond that there were no miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Submissive Man paid a few hu of grain per household and faced no other levies.

sentences.zh: 而宋人賦役嚴苦，貧者不復堪命，多逃亡入蠻。

translations.literal: But Song subjects' taxes and corvée were harsh; the poor could no longer bear it, and many fled into the Man lands.
translations.idiomatic: Song taxes and corvée were crushing; the poor could not endure them and fled into Man country in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 蠻無徭役，強者又不供官稅。

translations.literal: The Man had no corvée, and the strong among them also refused to pay official taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The Man owed no corvée, and their strong men refused state taxes.

sentences.zh: 結党連郡，動有數百千人，州郡力弱，則起為盜賊，種類稍多，戶口不可知也。

translations.literal: They formed factions linking whole commanderies; at a stroke they could muster hundreds or thousands. Where prefectures and commanderies were weak, they rose as bandits. As their clans multiplied, their households could no longer be counted.
translations.idiomatic: They banded together across commanderies, raising hundreds or thousands at a call. Where local power was weak they turned to brigandage. As clans multiplied, no one could number their households.

sentences.zh: 所在多深險。

translations.literal: Where they lived was mostly deep and perilous.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelt for the most part in deep, perilous country.

sentences.zh: 居武陵者有雄溪、樠溪、辰溪、酉溪、武溪，謂之五溪蠻。

translations.literal: Those in Wuling had the Xiong, Min, Chen, You, and Wu streams—called the Five Streams Man.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuling they held the Xiong, Min, Chen, You, and Wu streams—the Five Streams Man.

sentences.zh: 而宜都、天門、巴東、建平、江北諸郡蠻所居皆深山重阻，人跡罕至焉。

translations.literal: The Man of Yidu, Tianmen, Badong, Jianping, and the north-bank commanderies of Jiang all lived in mountains layered with barriers, where human tracks rarely reached.
translations.idiomatic: Man in Yidu, Tianmen, Badong, Jianping, and the north-bank Jiang commanderies lived behind mountain barriers where few travelers passed.

sentences.zh: 前世以來，屢為人患。

translations.literal: From former ages onward they were repeatedly a scourge to men.
translations.idiomatic: From ages past they had been a recurring scourge.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，宜都蠻帥石寧等一百二十三人詣闕上獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Shaodi's Jingping era, the Yidu Man chieftain Shi Ning and one hundred twenty-three others came to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping 2 of Emperor Shaodi, Yidu chieftain Shi Ning and 123 others came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉六年，建平蠻張維之等五十人，七年，宜都蠻田生等一百一十三人，並詣闕獻見。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Emperor Wen's Yuanjia era, fifty men of the Jianping Man led by Zhang Weizhi; in the seventh year, one hundred thirteen men of the Yidu Man led by Tian Sheng—all came to court and were received.
