translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 6, fifty Jianping Man led by Zhang Weizhi; in Yuanjia 7, 113 Yidu Man led by Tian Sheng—all came to court.

sentences.zh: 其後，沔中蠻大動，行旅殆絕。

translations.literal: Afterward the Man along the Mian rose in great commotion, and travelers on the roads nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Mian River Man rose in force and travel on the roads nearly stopped.

sentences.zh: 天門漊中令宋矯之徭賦過重，蠻不堪命。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Liaozhong in Tianmen, Song Jiaozhi, levied taxes and corvée too heavily; the Man could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jiaozhi, magistrate of Liaozhong in Tianmen, taxed and drafted too heavily; the Man could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，蠻田向求等為寇，破漊中，虜掠百姓。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Man Tian Xiangqiu and others raided, broke Liaozhong, and carried off the people.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, Tian Xiangqiu and other Man raided, overran Liaozhong, and seized the people.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史衡陽王義季遣行參軍曾孫念討破之，免矯之官。

translations.literal: Jingzhou inspector Prince Yiji of Hengyang sent the acting staff officer Zeng Sunnian to defeat them and removed Jiaozhi from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector Prince Yiji of Hengyang sent staff officer Zeng Sunnian to defeat them and dismissed Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 二十年，南郡臨沮、當陽蠻反，縛臨沮令傅僧驥。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Man of Linju and Dangyang in Nan commandery rebelled and bound the magistrate of Linju, Fu Sengji.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, Man of Linju and Dangyang in Nan commandery rebelled and seized the magistrate of Linju, Fu Sengji.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史南譙王義宣遣中兵參軍王諶討破之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou inspector Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao sent the central army staff officer Wang Chen to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao sent central-army staff officer Wang Chen to crush them.

sentences.zh: 先是，雍州刺史劉道產善撫諸蠻，前後不附者，皆引出平土，多緣沔為居。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yongzhou inspector Liu Daochan had been skilled at soothing the various Man; those who had not submitted before were all brought out to level ground, and many settled along the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yongzhou inspector Liu Daochan had soothed the Man well; those long unsubmissive were settled on level ground, many along the Mian.

sentences.zh: 及道產亡，蠻又反叛。

translations.literal: When Daochan died, the Man rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: When Daochan died, the Man rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 至孝武出為雍州，群蠻斷道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu went out to Yongzhou, the Man bands cut the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took up post in Yongzhou, Man bands cut the roads.

sentences.zh: 台遣軍主沈慶之連年討蠻，所向皆平，事在慶之傳。

translations.literal: The court sent the army commander Shen Qingzhi to campaign against the Man year after year; wherever he went he pacified them—the account is in Qingzhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent army commander Shen Qingzhi against the Man year after year; wherever he marched they were pacified—the full account is in his biography.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，龍山雉水蠻寇鈔涅陽縣，南陽太守朱韶遣軍討之，失利。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, the Longshan Zhishui Man raided Nieyang county; Nanyang prefect Zhu Shao sent troops against them and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 28, Longshan Zhishui Man raided Nieyang; Nanyang prefect Zhu Shao sent troops and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 韶又遣二千人系之，蠻乃散走。

translations.literal: Shao again sent two thousand men to pursue them, and the Man scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent another two thousand in pursuit, and the Man broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，滍水諸蠻因險為寇，雍州刺史隨王誕遣使說之，又遣軍討沔北諸蠻。

translations.literal: That year the Man along the Zhi used the terrain to raid; Yongzhou inspector Prince Dan of Sui sent envoys to persuade them and also sent troops against the Man north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhi River Man raided from the heights; Yongzhou inspector Prince Dan of Sui sent envoys to win them over and troops against the Man north of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 襲濁山、如口、蜀松三柴，克之，又圍鬥錢、柏義諸柴。

translations.literal: They stormed the three stockades of Zhuoshan, Rukou, and Shusong and took them, then besieged the stockades of Douqian, Boyi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the stockades at Zhuoshan, Rukou, and Shusong and took them, then besieged Douqian, Boyi, and other stockades.

sentences.zh: 蠻悉力距戰，軍大破之。

translations.literal: The Man resisted with all their strength; the army inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: The Man fought with all their strength; the army broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明中，建平蠻向光侯寇暴峽川，巴東太守王濟、荊州刺史朱修之遣軍討之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, the Jianping Man chieftain Xiang Guanghou raided and ravaged Xiachuan; Badong Administrator Wang Ji and Jingzhou Inspector Zhu Xiuzhi sent troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu in the Daming era, Jianping Man chieftain Xiang Guanghou ravaged Xiachuan; Badong administrator Wang Ji and Jingzhou inspector Zhu Xiuzhi sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 光侯走清江，清江去巴東千餘里。

translations.literal: Guanghou fled to the Qing River; the Qing River is more than a thousand li from Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghou fled to the Qing River, more than a thousand li from Badong.

sentences.zh: 時巴東、建平、宜都、天門四郡蠻為寇，諸郡人戶流散，百不存一。

translations.literal: At that time the Man of the four commanderies Badong, Jianping, Yidu, and Tianmen were raiding; households in the commanderies scattered until scarcely one in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Man of Badong, Jianping, Yidu, and Tianmen were then raiding in all four commanderies; households scattered until scarcely one in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 明帝、順帝世尤甚，荊州為之虛弊云。

translations.literal: Under Emperors Ming and Shun it was especially severe, and Jingzhou was left hollow and spent—so they say.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Shun the damage was worse still, and Jingzhou was left hollow and spent, so they say.

sentences.zh: 豫州蠻，稟君後也。

translations.literal: The Yuzhou Man were descendants of Lin Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuzhou Man were descended from Lin Jun.

sentences.zh: 盤瓠、稟君事，並具前史。

translations.literal: The matters of Panhu and Lin Jun are fully set forth in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: The stories of Panhu and Lin Jun are fully recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 西陽有巴水、蘄水、希水、赤亭水、西歸水，謂之五水蠻。

translations.literal: In Xiyang were the Ba River, Qi River, Xi River, Chiting River, and Xigui River—called the Five Waters Man.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiyang lay the Ba, Qi, Xi, Chiting, and Xigui rivers—the Five Waters Man.

sentences.zh: 所在並深岨，種落熾盛，曆世為盜賊。

translations.literal: Where they lived was all deep ravine; their tribes flourished, and for generations they had been brigands.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelt in deep ravines; their clans were strong, and for generations they had been brigands.

sentences.zh: 北接淮、汝，南極江、漢，地方數千里。

translations.literal: North they reached the Huai and Ru, south the utmost Jiang and Han—several thousand li in extent.
translations.idiomatic: North they reached the Huai and Ru, south the Jiang and Han—several thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉二十八年，西陽蠻殺南川令劉台。

translations.literal: In Song Yuanjia twenty-eighth year, Xiyang Man killed Nan commandery magistrate Liu Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia 28, Xiyang Man killed Nan commandery magistrate Liu Tai.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，新蔡蠻破大雷戍，略公私船入湖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Xincai Man broke Datile garrison and seized public and private boats on the lake.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, Xincai Man overran Datile garrison and seized public and private boats on the lake.

sentences.zh: 有亡命司馬黑石逃在蠻中，共為寇。

translations.literal: A fugitive, Sima Heishi, hid among the Man and together they raided.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive Sima Heishi hid among the Man and together they raided.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣太子步兵校尉沈慶之討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent the Crown Prince's infantry commandant Shen Qingzhi to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Crown Prince's infantry commandant Shen Qingzhi against them.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明四年，又遣慶之討西陽蠻，大克獲而反。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's fourth Daming year, Qingzhi was again sent against the Xiyang Man; he won a great victory and many captives and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowu's Daming 4, Qingzhi was again sent against the Xiyang Man and returned after a great victory and many captives.

sentences.zh: 司馬黑石徒黨三人，其一名智，黑石號曰太公，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Sima Heishi had three followers; one was named Zhi; Heishi styled himself Taigong and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Heishi had three followers: one named Zhi; Heishi styled himself Taigong and made him chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 一人名安陽，號譙王，一人名續之，號梁王。

translations.literal: One was named Anyang, styled King of Qiao; one was named Xuzhi, styled King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: One was named Anyang, styled King of Qiao; one was named Xuzhi, styled King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 蠻文山羅等討禽續之，為蠻世財所篡，山羅等相率斬世財父子六人。

translations.literal: The Man Wenshan Luo and others attacked and captured Xuzhi; he was set upon by the Man chieftain Shicai; Luo and the rest together beheaded Shicai father and son, six men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Man chieftain Wenshan Luo and others attacked and captured Xuzhi; the Man Shicai seized power; Luo and his men together beheaded Shicai and his six sons.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史王玄謨遣殿中將軍郭元封慰勞諸蠻，使縛送亡命。

translations.literal: Yuzhou Inspector Wang Xuanmo sent palace guard Guo Yuanfeng to console the various Man and ordered them to bind and send the fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou inspector Wang Xuanmo sent palace guard Guo Yuanfeng to console the Man and ordered them to bind and deliver the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 蠻乃執智、安陽二人，送詣玄謨。

translations.literal: The Man thereupon seized Zhi and Anyang and sent them to Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: The Man then seized Zhi and Anyang and sent them to Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 孝武使于壽陽斬之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had them beheaded at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had them beheaded at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國

translations.literal: States of the Western Regions
translations.idiomatic: States of the Western Regions

sentences.zh: 玉門以西達於西海，考之漢史，通為西域，高昌迄于波斯，則其所也。

translations.literal: From west of Yumen Gate to the Western Sea—in Han histories all called the Western Regions; from Gaochang to Persia marks their extent.
translations.idiomatic: West of Yumen Gate to the Western Sea—in Han histories all counted as the Western Regions; from Gaochang to Persia marks their reach.

sentences.zh: 自晉、宋以還，雖有時而至，論其風土，甚未能詳。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward envoys sometimes came, but their customs could not be set forth in much detail.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin and Song onward envoys sometimes arrived, but their lands and customs could not be described in much detail.

sentences.zh: 今略備西域諸國，編之於次云。

translations.literal: Here the states of the Western Regions are briefly recorded, set in order below.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions states are briefly recorded here, in the order that follows.

sentences.zh: 高昌國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Gaochang
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Gaochang

sentences.zh: 高昌國，初闞氏為主，其後為河西王沮渠茂虔弟無諱襲破之。

translations.literal: In Gaochang the Kan clan were first lords; later Wuwei, brother of Hexi King Juqu Maoqian, attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaochang the Kan clan first held sway; later Wuwei, brother of Hexi King Juqu Maoqian, attacked and overthrew them.

sentences.zh: 其王闞爽奔於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Their king Kan Shuang fled to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: King Kan Shuang fled to Rouran.

sentences.zh: 無諱據之稱王，一世而滅于魏。

translations.literal: Wuwei seized it and styled himself king; one generation later it was destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei seized the realm and styled himself king; one generation later Wei destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 其國人又推曲氏為王，名嘉，魏授為車騎將軍、司空公、都督秦州諸軍事、秦州刺史、金城郡公。

translations.literal: The people again raised the Qu clan to kingship—Jia by name; Wei made him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, area commander of Qinzhou, inspector of Qinzhou, and Duke of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The people again raised the Qu clan—Jia by name. Wei made him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, area commander of Qinzhou, inspector of Qinzhou, and Duke of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 在位二十四年卒，國諡曰昭武王。

translations.literal: He ruled twenty-four years and died; the state posthumously titled him Bright Martial King.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled twenty-four years and died; the state gave him the posthumous title Bright Martial King.

sentences.zh: 子子堅，子堅嗣位，魏授使持節、驃騎大將軍、散騎常侍、都督瓜州刺史、西平郡公、開府儀同三司、高昌王。

translations.literal: His son Zijian succeeded; Wei granted him bearer of the staff, General of Flying Cavalry, regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of Guazhou, Duke of Xiping, equal in glory to the Three Dukes, and King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zijian succeeded; Wei made him bearer of the staff, General of Flying Cavalry, regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of Guazhou, Duke of Xiping, equal in glory to the Three Dukes, and King of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 其國蓋車師之故地，南接河南，東近敦煌，西次龜茲，北鄰敕勒。

translations.literal: The state was roughly the old land of Cheshi; south it adjoined Henan, east it neared Dunhuang, west it reached Kucha, north it neighbored the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was roughly old Cheshi territory: south it adjoined Henan, east it neared Dunhuang, west it reached Kucha, north it bordered the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 置四十六鎮，交河田地高寧臨川橫截柳婆洿林新興由甯始昌篤進白力等鎮。

translations.literal: It set up forty-six garrisons—Jiaohe, Tiandi, Gaoning, Linchuan, Hengjie, Liupo, Wulin, Xinxing, Youning, Shichang, Dujin, Baili, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: It maintained forty-six garrisons—Jiaohe, Tiandi, Gaoning, Linchuan, Hengjie, Liupo, Wulin, Xinxing, Youning, Shichang, Dujin, Baili, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 官有四鎮將軍，及置雜號將軍、長史、司馬、門下校郎、中兵校郎、通事舍人、通事令史、諮議、諫議、校尉、主簿。

translations.literal: Offices included four-garrison generals and miscellaneous-title generals, chief clerks, marshals, gate-section adjutants, central-army adjutants, liaison attendants, liaison clerks, advisers, remonstrators, commandants, and chief recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included four-garrison generals and miscellaneous-title generals, chief clerks, marshals, gate-section adjutants, central-army adjutants, liaison attendants, liaison clerks, advisers, remonstrators, commandants, and chief recorders.

sentences.zh: 國人言語與華略同。

translations.literal: The people's speech was roughly like that of China.
translations.idiomatic: The people's speech was roughly like that of China.

sentences.zh: 有五經、歷代史、諸子集。

translations.literal: They had the Five Classics, dynastic histories, and collected works of the masters.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed the Five Classics, dynastic histories, and collected works of the masters.

sentences.zh: 面貌類高麗，辮髪垂之於背。

translations.literal: Their faces resembled Goguryeo's; hair was braided and hung down the back.
translations.idiomatic: Their faces resembled Goguryeo's; hair was braided and hung down the back.

sentences.zh: 著長身小袖袍、縵襠褲。

translations.literal: They wore long-bodied small-sleeved robes and patterned trousers.
translations.idiomatic: They wore long-bodied small-sleeved robes and patterned trousers.

sentences.zh: 女子頭髮，辮而不垂，著錦纈纓絡環釧。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair without letting it hang, and wore brocade head ornaments, chains, rings, and bracelets.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair without letting it hang, and wore brocade head ornaments, chains, rings, and bracelets.

sentences.zh: 昏姻有六禮。

translations.literal: Marriage had the six rites.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage followed the six rites.

sentences.zh: 其地高燥，築土為城，架木為屋，土覆其上。

translations.literal: The land was high and dry; they built cities of earth, framed houses of wood, and roofed them with earth.
translations.idiomatic: The land was high and dry; they built earthen cities, framed houses of wood, and roofed them with earth.

sentences.zh: 寒暑與益州相似，備植九穀，人多噉面及牛羊肉。

translations.literal: Cold and heat resembled Yizhou's; they planted all nine grains; people mostly ate griddle-cakes, mutton, and beef.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat were much like Yizhou's; they planted all nine grains; people mostly ate griddle-cakes, mutton, and beef.

sentences.zh: 出良馬、蒲桃酒、石鹽。

translations.literal: They produced fine horses, grape wine, and rock salt.
translations.idiomatic: They produced fine horses, grape wine, and rock salt.

sentences.zh: 多草木，有草實如繭，繭中絲如細纑，名曰白疊子，國人取織以為布。

translations.literal: Grass and trees were abundant; grass seed pods were like cocoons, and the silk inside was like fine floss—called white pile seed; people gathered them to weave cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees were abundant; grass seed came in pods like cocoons, with silk inside fine as floss—called white pile seed—and people wove it into cloth.

sentences.zh: 布甚軟白，交市用焉。

translations.literal: The cloth was very soft and white, used in trade.
translations.idiomatic: The cloth was very soft and white and served in trade.

sentences.zh: 有朝烏者，旦旦集王殿前，為行列，不畏人，日出然後散去。

translations.literal: There were court-birds—each dawn they assembled before the royal hall in ranks, unafraid of people, and only dispersed after sunrise.
translations.idiomatic: There were court-birds: each dawn they gathered before the royal hall in ranks, unafraid of people, and only scattered after sunrise.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，子堅遣使獻鳴鹽枕、蒲桃、良馬、氍獀等物。

translations.literal: In Liang's Datong era, Zijian sent envoys presenting singing-salt pillows, grapes, fine horses, carpets, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era, Zijian sent envoys with singing-salt pillows, grapes, fine horses, carpets, and the like.

sentences.zh: 魏之居代都，滑猶為小國，屬蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When Wei dwelt at the capital in Dai, Hua was still a small state, subject to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei dwelt at Dai, Hua was still a small state under Rouran.

sentences.zh: 後稍強大，征其旁國波斯、渴盤陀、罽賓、焉耆、龜茲、疏勒、姑墨、于闐、句般等國，開地千餘里。

translations.literal: Later it grew somewhat powerful, campaigning against neighboring states—Persia, Kepantuo, Kasmira, Karasahr, Kucha, Shule, Gumo, Yutian, Gupan, and others—opening territory over a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Later it grew stronger and campaigned against neighboring states—Persia, Kepantuo, Kasmira, Karasahr, Kucha, Shule, Gumo, Yutian, Gupan, and others—opening territory over a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 土地溫暖，多山川，少樹木，有五穀。

translations.literal: The land was warm; mountains and rivers were many, trees few; there were the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land was warm, with many mountains and rivers but few trees; the five grains grew there.

sentences.zh: 國人以面及羊肉為糧。

translations.literal: The people used flour and mutton as food.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived on flour and mutton.

sentences.zh: 其獸有師子、兩腳駱駝，野驢有角。

translations.literal: Their beasts included lions and two-legged camels; wild asses had horns.
translations.idiomatic: Their beasts included lions and two-legged camels; wild asses bore horns.

sentences.zh: 人皆善騎射，著小袖長身袍，用金玉為帶。

translations.literal: All were skilled at riding and archery; they wore small-sleeved long-bodied robes, with belts of gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: All were skilled riders and archers; they wore small-sleeved long-bodied robes with belts of gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 女人被裘，頭上刻木為角，長六尺，以金銀飾之。

translations.literal: Women wore furs; on their heads they carved wooden horns six feet long, adorned with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore furs and carved wooden horns six feet long for their heads, adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 少女子，兄弟共妻。

translations.literal: There were few women; brothers shared wives.
translations.idiomatic: Women were scarce; brothers shared a wife.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，氈屋為居，東向開戶。

translations.literal: There were no walled cities—they lived in felt tents, doors opening east.
translations.idiomatic: They had no walled cities and lived in felt tents with doors facing east.

sentences.zh: 其王坐金床，隨太歲轉，與妻並坐接客。

translations.literal: Their king sat on a golden bed, turning with the Grand Year Star, and received guests seated together with his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Their king sat on a golden bed that turned with the Grand Year Star and received guests seated beside his wife.

sentences.zh: 無文字，以木為契。

translations.literal: They had no writing; wood served as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing and used wood for tokens.

sentences.zh: 與旁國通，則使旁國胡為胡書，羊皮為紙。

translations.literal: When dealing with neighboring states, they had neighboring barbarians write in barbarian script, sheepskin serving as paper.
translations.idiomatic: When dealing with neighbors, they had neighboring barbarians write in barbarian script on sheepskin for paper.

sentences.zh: 無職官。

translations.literal: There were no official posts.
translations.idiomatic: They had no official posts.

sentences.zh: 事天神、火神，每日則出戶祀神而後食。

translations.literal: They served Heaven-god and Fire-god; each day they left the door to worship the gods before eating.
translations.idiomatic: They served Heaven-god and Fire-god; each day they went out to worship before eating.

sentences.zh: 其跪一拜而止。

translations.literal: Their kneeling bow was one prostration and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Their kneeling bow was a single prostration and no more.

sentences.zh: 葬以木為槨。

translations.literal: Burial used wooden coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Burial was in wooden coffins.

sentences.zh: 父母死，其子截一耳，葬訖即吉。

translations.literal: When parents died, their sons cut off one ear; mourning ended as soon as burial was done.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, sons cut off one ear; mourning ended as soon as burial was finished.

sentences.zh: 其言語待河南人譯然後通。

translations.literal: Their speech required Henan people as interpreters before it could be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech had to be rendered by Henan interpreters before it could be understood.

sentences.zh: 呵跋檀、周古柯、胡密丹等國，並滑旁小國也。

translations.literal: He Batan, Zhou Guke, Hu Midan, and other states were all small states beside Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He Batan, Zhou Guke, Hu Midan, and other states were all small kingdoms beside Hua.

sentences.zh: 凡滑旁之國，衣服容貌皆與滑同。

translations.literal: All states beside Hua—clothing and faces all matched Hua's.
translations.idiomatic: All states beside Hua wore the same clothes and looked the same as Hua.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，使使隨滑使來貢獻方物。

translations.literal: In Putong 1, envoys came with Hua's embassy to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 envoys came with Hua's embassy to present tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 白題國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Baiti
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Baiti

sentences.zh: 白題國王姓支名史稽毅，其先蓋匈奴之別種胡也。

translations.literal: In Baiti the king's surname was Zhi, name Shi Jiyi; his ancestors were likely a separate branch of the Xiongnu barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Baiti the king's surname was Zhi and his name Shi Jiyi; his ancestors were likely a separate branch of the Xiongnu barbarians.

sentences.zh: 漢灌嬰與匈奴戰，斬白題騎一人是也。

translations.literal: In Han, Guan Ying fought the Xiongnu and cut down one Baiti horseman—that is the reference.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Guan Ying fought the Xiongnu and cut down one Baiti horseman—that is the origin of the name.

sentences.zh: 在滑國東，去滑六日行，西極波斯。

translations.literal: It lies east of Hua, six days' travel from Hua; west it reaches as far as Persia.
translations.idiomatic: It lies east of Hua, six days' travel away; west it reaches as far as Persia.

sentences.zh: 土地出粟、麥、瓜果，食物略與滑同。

translations.literal: The land produced millet, wheat, melons, and fruits; food was roughly like Hua's.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced millet, wheat, melons, and fruits; food was much like Hua's.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 3 they sent envoys with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Kucha
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Kucha

sentences.zh: 龜茲者，西域之舊國也。

translations.literal: Kucha was an ancient state of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was an old kingdom of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 自晉度江不通，至梁普通二年，王尼瑞摩珠那勝遣使奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: From Jin's crossing of the river there was no contact until Liang Putong 2, when King Niruimozhunasheng sent envoys with a memorial and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin crossed the river contact ceased until Liang Putong 2, when King Niruimozhunasheng sent envoys with a formal tribute memorial.

sentences.zh: 于闐國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Yutian
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Yutian

sentences.zh: 于闐者，西域之舊國也。

translations.literal: Yutian was an ancient state of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Yutian was an old kingdom of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 梁天監九年，始通江左，遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In Liang Tianjian 9 they first opened relations with the Jiangzuo court and sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Tianjian 9 they first opened relations with the court south of the Yangzi and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又獻波羅婆步鄣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they again presented a prasada hanging screen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 they again offered a prasada screen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，又獻琉璃罌。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year they again presented a glass jar.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 they sent a glass vessel.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，又獻外國刻玉佛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, they again presented a foreign carved jade Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 they sent a foreign-carved jade Buddha.

sentences.zh: 渴盤陀國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Kepantuo
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Kepantuo

sentences.zh: 渴盤陀國，于闐西小國也。

translations.literal: The state of Kepantuo is a small state west of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Kepantuo was a small kingdom west of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 西鄰滑國，南接罽賓國，北連沙勒。

translations.literal: West it borders Hua; south it adjoins Jibin; north it connects with Shale.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Hua to the west, Jibin to the south, and Shale to the north.

sentences.zh: 國都在山谷中，城周回十餘里。

translations.literal: Its seat lies in a mountain valley; the city wall runs over ten li round.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital stood in a mountain valley, walled for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 國有十二城，風俗與于闐相類。

translations.literal: The state has twelve cities; customs resemble Khotan's.
translations.idiomatic: The realm held twelve towns; its customs were much like Khotan's.

sentences.zh: 衣古貝布，著長身小袖袍、小口褲。

translations.literal: They wear kapok cloth, long-bodied small-sleeved robes, and narrow trousers.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed in kapok cloth, long tight-sleeved coats, and narrow trousers.

sentences.zh: 地宜小麥，資以為糧。

translations.literal: The land suits wheat, which supplies their grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat flourished there and fed the people.

sentences.zh: 多牛馬駱駝羊等。

translations.literal: Cattle, horses, camels, sheep, and the like are many.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle, horses, camels, and sheep were abundant.

sentences.zh: 出好氈。

translations.literal: It produces fine felt.
translations.idiomatic: It yielded fine felt.

sentences.zh: 王姓葛沙氏，梁中大同元年，始通江左，遣獻方物。

translations.literal: The royal surname is Gesa; in Liang Zhongdatong 1 they first opened relations with Jiangzuo and sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Gesa; in Liang Zhongdatong 1 they first opened relations with the court south of the Yangzi and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 末國，漢世且末國也。

translations.literal: The state of Mo was Han-era Qimo.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was the Han-era kingdom of Qimo.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Fighting men exceed ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than ten thousand fighting households.

sentences.zh: 北與丁零、東與白題、西與波斯接。

translations.literal: North it borders Dingling; east Baiti; west Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Dingling lay to the north, Baiti to the east, and Persia to the west.

sentences.zh: 土人剪發，著氊帽、小袖衣，為衫則開頸而縫前。

translations.literal: Natives crop their hair, wear felt caps and small-sleeved coats; when making a jacket they open the neck and sew the front closed.
translations.idiomatic: The people cropped their hair, wore felt caps and short-sleeved coats, and stitched their tunics closed at the neck and front.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊騾驢。

translations.literal: Sheep, cattle, mules, and donkeys are many.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep, cattle, mules, and donkeys were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 其王安末深盤，梁普通五年，始通江左，遣使來貢獻。

translations.literal: Its king Anmo Shenpan—in Liang Putong 5 first opened relations with Jiangzuo and sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Anmo Shenpan first opened relations with the court south of the Yangzi in Liang Putong 5 and sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 波斯國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Persia
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Persia

sentences.zh: 波斯國，其先有波斯匿王者，子孫以王父字為氏，因為國號。

translations.literal: Persia: formerly there was a king named Bosini; descendants took their father's name character as surname, hence the state's name.
translations.idiomatic: Persia took its name from an early king called Bosini, whose descendants adopted his personal name as their clan surname.

sentences.zh: 國有城周回三十二里，城高四丈，皆有樓觀。

translations.literal: The state had a walled city, thirty-two li in circuit, walls four zhang high, all with towered pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital ran thirty-two li around, with walls four zhang high and towered watchposts.

sentences.zh: 城內屋宇數百千間，城外佛寺二三百所。

translations.literal: Within the city were hundreds of thousands of buildings; outside were two or three hundred Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood hundreds of thousands of houses, and outside two or three hundred Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 西去城十五里有土山，山非過高，其勢連接甚遠。

translations.literal: Fifteen li west of the city is an earthen mountain—not especially high, but its ridges stretch far.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li west stood a low earthen ridge running far.

sentences.zh: 中有鷲鳥噉羊，土人極以為患。

translations.literal: Vultures there devour sheep, and the natives find it a grave affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Vultures there preyed on sheep, and the people counted it a great plague.

sentences.zh: 國中有優缽曇花，鮮華可愛。

translations.literal: In the state is the udumbara flower—fresh and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: The udumbara flower grew there, bright and fair.

sentences.zh: 出龍駒馬。

translations.literal: Dragon colts are produced.
translations.idiomatic: It bred dragon colts.

sentences.zh: 咸池生珊瑚樹，長一二尺。

translations.literal: At Xianchi coral trees grow, one or two feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Coral trees grew at Xianchi, a foot or two in height.

sentences.zh: 亦有武魄、馬腦、真珠、玫瑰等，國內不以為珍。

translations.literal: There are also amber, carnelian, pearls, and rose quartz—these are not considered precious within the country.
translations.idiomatic: Amber, carnelian, pearls, and rose quartz were common and not prized at home.

sentences.zh: 市買用金銀。

translations.literal: Market trade uses gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Markets traded in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 昏姻法，下娉財訖，女婿將數十人迎婦。

translations.literal: Marriage law: after the bride-price is settled, the son-in-law leads several dozen men to welcome the bride.
translations.idiomatic: By marriage custom, once the bride-price was paid the groom led dozens of men to fetch the bride.

sentences.zh: 婿著金線錦袍、師子錦褲，戴天冠。

translations.literal: The groom wears gold-thread brocade robe and lion brocade trousers, crowned with a heavenly cap.
translations.idiomatic: The groom wore gold-thread brocade and lion-pattern trousers with a heavenly crown.

sentences.zh: 婦亦如之。

translations.literal: The bride likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The bride wore the same.

sentences.zh: 婦兄弟便來捉手付度，夫婦之禮，于茲永畢。

translations.literal: The bride's brothers at once come and take her by the hand to give her over—the rites of husband and wife are from this forever complete.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers then took her hand and passed her to the groom—the wedding rites ended there.

sentences.zh: 國東與滑國、西及南俱與娑羅門國、北與泛栗國接。

translations.literal: East it borders Hua; west and south alike Brahman; north Fanli.
translations.idiomatic: Hua lay to the east; Brahman to the west and south; Fanli to the north.

sentences.zh: 梁中大通二年，始通江左，遣使獻佛牙。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong under Liang, they first opened relations with the Jiangzuo court and sent envoys presenting a Buddha tooth.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, in Zhongdatong 2 they first dealt with the lands south of the Yangzi and sent a Buddha tooth as tribute.

sentences.zh: 北狄種類實繁，蠕蠕為族，蓋匈奴之別種也。

translations.literal: Northern Di peoples were indeed numerous; the Rouran were one such tribe, probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Di peoples were many; the Rouran were one tribe, likely a separate branch of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 魏自南遷，因擅其故地。

translations.literal: After Wei moved south, they seized its former lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei moved south, the Rouran took over its old territory.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，隨水草畜牧，以穹廬居。

translations.literal: They had no walled cities; they followed water and grass in herding livestock and dwelled in yurt tents.
translations.idiomatic: They had no cities, followed pasture and water with their herds, and lived in felt yurts.

sentences.zh: 辮髪，衣錦小袖袍、小口褲、深雍韡。

translations.literal: They wore braided hair, brocade small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and deep boots.
translations.idiomatic: They braided their hair and dressed in brocade small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and deep boots.

sentences.zh: 其地苦寒，七月流澌亙河。

translations.literal: The land was bitterly cold; in the seventh month floating ice spanned the rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The country was bitterly cold; in the seventh month ice floes bridged the rivers.

sentences.zh: 其國能以術祭天而致風雪，前對皎日，後則泥潦橫流，故其戰敗莫能追及。

translations.literal: Their state can by art sacrifice to Heaven and bring wind and snow; facing it one meets bright sun, behind one muddy flood streams across—thus when they are defeated none can pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran could perform rituals to Heaven and summon wind and snow; bright sun lay ahead while muddy floods swept behind, so when they broke and fled no pursuer could catch them.

sentences.zh: 或於中夏為之，則不能雨，問其故，蓋以暖云。

translations.literal: If performed within Central China, then it could not rain; asked the reason, they said it was because of warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Performed in China proper, the rite brought no rain; asked why, they said the land was too warm.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自晉氏南度，介居江左，北荒西裔，隔礙莫通。

translations.literal: Discussion: From the time Jin moved south and established itself on the Jiangzuo, the northern wastes and western borderlands were cut off and unreachable.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: After the Jin court moved south and held only the Jiangzuo, the northern frontier and western marches were blocked off and out of reach.

sentences.zh: 至於南徼東邊。

translations.literal: As for the southern frontier and eastern marches.
translations.idiomatic: As for the southern frontier and eastern marches,

sentences.zh: 界壤所接，洎宋元嘉撫運，爰命干戈，象浦之捷，威震冥海。

translations.literal: Where borders met, down through Song Yuanjia when the throne took up arms—the victory at Xiangpu shook the Dark Sea.
translations.idiomatic: where borders adjoined—by Song Yuanjia, when the throne took up arms, the victory at Xiangpu made the Dark Sea tremble.

sentences.zh: 於是鞮譯相系，無絕歲時。

translations.literal: Then interpreters and envoys followed one another without cease year-round.
translations.idiomatic: Then interpreters and envoys followed one another without a break through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 以洎齊、梁，職貢有序。

translations.literal: On through Qi and Liang, tribute duties kept their order.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qi and Liang, tribute and office kept their proper order.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，邊鄙日蹙。

translations.literal: At the turmoil of Hou Jing the frontier daily shrank.
translations.idiomatic: With the turmoil of Hou Jing the frontier shrank day by day.

sentences.zh: 陳氏基命，衰微已甚，救首救尾，身其幾何。

translations.literal: When Chen received the Mandate, decline was already extreme—saving head or tail, how long could it last?
translations.idiomatic: When Chen received the Mandate, decline was already extreme—whether one saved head or tail, how long could it endure?

sentences.zh: 故西贐南琛，無聞竹素，豈所謂有德則來，無道則去者也。

translations.literal: Thus western tribute and southern jewels ceased to appear in the bamboo registers—is this not what is meant by "if there is virtue they come; if there is no Way they go"?
translations.idiomatic: Thus western gifts and southern treasures no longer reached the bamboo annals—was this not the saying that virtue draws men in and the lack of the Way sends them away?
